stem: A patient has nocturnal tingling in the thumb, index and middle fingers with preserved sensation over the thenar eminence. Where is the lesion most likely?

options.label: A
options.explanation: This compresses the ulnar nerve and affects the little finger and ulnar half of the ring finger.

options.label: B
options.explanation: A proximal median lesion can involve the palmar cutaneous branch and produce broader forearm or palm symptoms.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Compression affects median-nerve fibres destined for the digital sensory and thenar motor branches. The palmar cutaneous branch bypasses the tunnel, so thenar skin sensation is usually spared.

options.label: D
options.explanation: This affects the ulnar nerve at the wrist, not the lateral three-and-a-half digits.

options.label: E
options.explanation: This affects radial-nerve motor branches and does not produce this median sensory distribution.

context: The spared thenar eminence points to a lesion distal to the palmar cutaneous branch, which passes superficial to the flexor retinaculum.
